commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[eval] Preserve Iris capability URLs in Harbor jobs (#8803)

Marin rebuilt Harbor's live `JobConfig` by serializing and revalidating
it. Harbor correctly redacted the Iris capability token during
serialization, so the live agent received a literal `<redacted>` URL and
every request returned 401.

Keep the already validated models live, and convert only `jobs_dir` to
Harbor's required `UPath`. Serialized configs still redact the dummy
token. This changes Marin only; stable Harbor remains
`83709b4aa03c2b9a92d8d78a8c12157b31d1e461`, with no pin change or
promotion.

Local evidence:

- The focused regression failed before the fix because the live
`api_base` contained `<redacted>`, then passed with the exact dummy
capability URL live and the token absent from `model_dump(mode="json")`.
- The final focused regression passed and also proved `jobs_dir /
job_name` composes.
- The integration file reported 14 passed and 1 failed. The sole failure
is the unchanged `attempt_index` mismatch in
`test_terminus_policies_retry_transient_endpoint_errors`; this PR does
not change it.
- The affected runner and full pre-commit gate passed. Semantic review
found no issues.
- High-tier GOAL review found no material candidate issue in the
successful Claude and Codex passes. Gemini was unavailable after one
bounded retry.

Production evidence at exact Marin
`f163302dfbcedddbf83e01543e0894d5a2338c0c` and stable Harbor
`83709b4aa03c2b9a92d8d78a8c12157b31d1e461`:

- AIME run `20260831-040512-qwen3-0.6b-aime-smoke-3b20` completed
successfully on `v5litepod-4` in `us-west4`.
- Coverage was 8/8 scored (100%), with no unanswered items or recorded
errors.
- Metrics were nonempty: attempted 8, total 8, accuracy 0.0, mean reward
0.0, and solved 0.0.
- The complete 1,556-line Iris log contained eight successful evaluation
requests and no `401` or `Unauthorized`.
- The orchestrator is terminal succeeded, the inference child is
terminal after launcher cleanup, and the exact prefix has no running
jobs.
- Durable record:
`gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals/20260831-040512-qwen3-0.6b-aime-smoke-3b20/record.json`.

The earlier run at `88978b607f` failed on `jobs_dir` before creating a
trial or making an evaluation request. Its lack of 401 text was not
authentication evidence.

Echo incident: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/290

Part of #8323

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Make ragged all-to-all the hero EP default on the pinned XLA-fork PJRT build (#8684)

This PR swaps the EP backend for the in-flight GB200 hero run to the
updated ragged all-to-all backend added in #8549. The latter requires a
[patched PJRT
wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/commit/ead1cd5a104a6f7ab7760835a2ab1260915babf3),
pinned here.

### Notes

- Drops the FP32 pinned-host master params needed by the current
pooled-wave backend, keeping fp32 weights on device (+0.4 pp MFU). Note:
this introduces a complication in that the **checkpoint format is
incompatible with the current hero** (the latter contains a master
params leaf in the state tree). We mitigate this by detecting and
automatically migrating checkpoints in the old format.
- The H100 ladder keeps pooled-wave; enabling the performant ragged
backend on H100 requires additional work, as the expert MLP is
specialized to SM100 and the patched PJRT wheel currently built for
aarch64 only; `small_scale_abl_launch` keeps both as separate arms since
it measures the comparison.
- Resume attempts that find checkpoints and load none of them now fail
loudly instead of silently restarting at step 0. This was motivated by
several mishaps in the development of this branch where failed restores
resulted in (silent) fallbacks to random initialization.

### Pre-merge checklist

- [x] Promote the 0.11.1-based forked-PJRT wheel (build:
https://github.com/marin-community/xla/actions/runs/33191707103/job/98918546868)
- [x] Re-pin the promoted wheel: swap the `jax-cuda13-pjrt` source URL
in `lib/marin/pyproject.toml`, `uv lock`, confirm CI green including
`test_the_patched_pjrt_wheel_pairs_with_the_pinned_jax`
- [x] One-rack diagnostic restored from the latest hero checkpoint; loss
continuous across the restart
- [x] Confirm expected MFU and drop rate at rack scale ~22.5--23% /
<0.05%
- [x] Confirm device peak stays under the 138.2 GiB `cuda_async` release
threshold (#8490)
- [ ] Restart the production hero at S=~200 steps past a checkpoint from
this branch, monitor loss/drops for S steps

On success: merge PR. On failure at any step: restart production hero
from last run commit and its own checkpoint. The old code restores the
pre-conversion checkpoints unchanged.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Run the ragged EP weight gradients on QuACK and delete the cuDNN path (#8814)

Supersedes #8793. That PR pads expert groups to the size the cuDNN
grouped-Wgrad kernel declares. This PR deletes the kernel instead.

- **Both expert weight gradients move to QuACK's varlen-k grouping.**
They contract over the ragged dimension and need `cu_seqlens_k`. QuACK's
SM100 GEMM supports that grouping, but the vendored shim passed only
`cu_seqlens_m`.
- **Throughput rises 0.81 MFU, or 4.1% more tokens per second**, against
a control that computes the same gradients correctly.
- **The `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` dependency goes away**, with one of the
two grouped-GEMM kernel families and a 148-line module.
- **Issue #8339 closes by construction.** The padding existed only to
satisfy cuDNN.

The change replaces a copy, not arithmetic. cuDNN counts tiles per
expert from that expert's row count, but addresses through one
descriptor over the whole buffer. Every group must therefore start on a
256-row boundary. The wrapper met that by copying both multi-GB operands
into an aligned layout on every call, at 365 ms per step. QuACK offsets
a coordinate into the descriptor instead.

The tile setting carries the result. At the default tile QuACK is slower
than cuDNN. At tile (256, 256) with cluster (2, 2, 1) it runs the two
calls in 7.22 and 3.41 ms, against 10.15 and 4.68. Those cuDNN figures
come from the corrected 256-row wrapper, not the 8-row wrapper on
`main`. The 8-row wrapper is cheaper because it reads past each group.

Read the line count carefully. Runtime backend source loses 120 lines of
code and gains 143 lines of comment, for a raw net of -23. The whole
change adds 380 lines, because it also adds a 142-line test file and a
296-line benchmark. Neither existed before: this kernel path had no
tests.

Both kernels take bf16, accumulate in fp32, and write bf16. Only the
reduction order changes. The 4-GPU ragged-EP gate reproduces #8793's
corrected gradient column to three significant figures on all four
seeds, at the ring backend's own floor. Drop counts match the capacity
model exactly. New SM100 tests cover uneven, tile-unaligned, and
empty-group splits, and pass 9 of 9 on GB200.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Complete the controller-backend phase boundary (#8762)

Make `Controller` the sole owner of Iris persistence, worker liveness,
lifecycle policy, and phase sequencing. `TaskBackend` now receives
complete request records for initialization, scheduling, reconciliation,
observation, autoscaling, and capacity removal. It returns decisions,
exact runtime observations, or provider effects without receiving a
controller database, transaction, transition reader, or liveness
tracker.

Worker and Kubernetes reconciliation now produce the same exact
task-attempt facts. The controller reloads state after provider I/O,
fences each observation by Attempt UID, applies one lifecycle path, and
commits before requesting physical capacity removal. Status and capacity
are published on the control thread from controller-supplied facts;
autoscaler recovery and updates return state for the controller to
persist.

Delete `BackendRuntime` and `DbBackendWorkerStore`, and separate
provisioning from worker teardown. The branch removes 1,824 lines and
adds 1,536. RPC schemas and client behavior are unchanged. The
controller, backend, and lifecycle journey suites pass 1,240 tests;
repository formatting, Ruff, and Pyrefly checks pass.

---------

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fix the GCP tunnel port and parallelize shard existence probes (#8817)

Four independent fixes across iris, levanter, marin, and zephyr.

`GcpControllerProvider.tunnel` accepted an `address` argument and
discarded it,
hardcoding `localhost:10000` as the SSH forward target. A cluster that
sets
`controller.gcp.port` to anything else got a tunnel pointed at a dead
port, even
though `discover_controller` in the same class honors the setting and
the
Kubernetes provider parses the port out of `address`. The GCP path now
parses the
remote port from the address and threads it through the tunnel helpers.
Both
address forms reach `tunnel`: the bare `host:port` that
`discover_controller`
returns and the `http://host:port` that the start and restart paths
return.

`_mk_shard_name_mapping` in levanter probed `StoragePath(url).exists()`
once per
expanded shard URL in a serial loop, only to build a missing-shard
warning. It
runs eagerly from `UrlBackedShardedDataSource.__init__`, so a mixture
component
naming thousands of GCS shards paid thousands of sequential object-store
round
trips per host at startup. The probes now run on a 32-thread pool and
are zipped
back to their URLs in order, leaving the mapping, the duplicate-name
error, and
the warning unchanged.

`convert_page` in marin has rejected every `extract_method` value except
"resiliparse" since #2232 deleted the readability and trafilatura
extractors in
December 2025. The parameter is gone, along with its ValueError branch
and the
plumbing that carried it through four transform config dataclasses and
their call
sites. `convert_page` was then a one-line delegation to
`convert_page_with_resiliparse`, so the two collapse into the single
`convert_page` entry point already exported from `marin.web`.

`ZephyrContext._start_pool` held a verbatim copy of the teardown
sequence in
`_OwnedPool.shutdown`: `stop_workers` at a 30s deadline,
`coordinator.shutdown`
at 10s, then the actor group, each suppressed. Startup now builds the
`_OwnedPool` as soon as the coordinator handle exists and tears it down
through
that one method, so the RPC order and its timeouts have one definition.
Two
`assert self.client is not None` statements ahead of `pool.shutdown()`
are
removed; the argument they guarded went away when `shutdown` lost its
client
parameter in #8080.

---------

[grafana] Remove CoreWeave ferry minimum duration (#8811)

Stop classifying successful CoreWeave ferry runs as unhealthy solely
because they finish in under 15 minutes. Scheduled run
[33317151515](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33317151515)
completed in 834 seconds; submission, execution, and metric validation
all passed.

still requires successful job completion, at least 40 training steps,
and loss at or below 10.0.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Fix Megablox tiling across ragged-dot gradients (#8719)

The production failure and the later v5e CI failure had different
causes.

Haliax now passes Megablox a tiling policy instead of freezing the
forward GMM tile. JAX evaluates the policy for each transformed GMM, so
forward and VJP calls each clamp their real `(m, k, n)` dimensions. The
existing accelerator MoE regression forces Megablox on TPU and checks
BF16 values, input gradients, weight gradients, finiteness, and overflow
behavior for both `ring` and `ragged_a2a` expert parallelism.

The full v5e lane then exposed an unrelated pytest collection leak.
Three test modules changed process-wide JAX matmul precision at import
time. Collecting one of them was enough to turn the later BF16 Megablox
lowering into FP32 and trigger Mosaic's `Bad lhs type`. Precision
changes are now scoped to module fixtures, and the one strict downstream
oracle requests FP32 inside its own test. No v5-only tile, workflow
diagnostic, selector change, or VMEM workaround remains.

The squashed head `7339f798597a748ab090a20d2d106c24a7392a35` has Git
tree `7c2b8ce49c7213930cc2ef02c37f84753602fbfb`, identical to qualified
head `3dfe45750805f484fa378e952b7924a6f51d9f3b`; `git diff` between the
two heads is empty. At that qualified tree:

- The [authoritative v5e
workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33293007271)
and [TPU
job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33293007271/job/99207863146)
passed both target variants and the full fixed lane: `1074 passed, 30
skipped, 171 deselected`.
- The one exact blank-input [canary
ferry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33294173253)
succeeded on production-priority preemptible v6e-4. Its [Iris
child](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frunner%2Firis-run-job-20260830-051314%2Fgrug-train-canary-tpu-33294173253-1)
completed 238/238 steps with zero preemptions; the unchanged validator
passed 237 recorded steps and final loss `5.7976 <= 8.0`.
- The canary preserved its [W&B
run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/canary-tpu-33294173253-1)
and [direct XProf
trace](https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/xprof/open?uri=gs%3A%2F%2Fmarin-eu-west4%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Fcanary-tpu-33294173253-1&tool=trace_viewer).
- Changed-file checks, focused local regressions, and two independent
High-reasoning reviews passed with no material findings.

The resolved CI collection incident and response are preserved in [Echo
wiki #291](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/291).

Fixes #8731.
Unblocks #8718.

commits.message:
[grafana] Preserve collector failures at counter boundaries (#8799)

Mark collector health `incomplete` when a positive in-window
stage-failure sample has no predecessor in the bounded scan. Keep that
value out of the numeric failure total because its pre-window portion is
unknown.

Count a positive post-reset value as the definite contribution since the
reset. Ordinary increases keep `value - previous_value`; shared token,
outcome, histogram, and preemption counter rules are unchanged.

On current `origin/main`, both boundary regressions reported `healthy`;
the final focused suite passes 19 tests. The generated SQL passed the
production Finelog planner and returned the ordered ten-column response.

Fixes #8798

Co-authored-by: yoblin <268258002+yoblin@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[grafana] Remove TPU ferry minimum duration (#8801)

Stop classifying successful TPU ferry runs as unhealthy solely because
they
finish in under one hour. A [healthy
run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33294173253)
completed
in about 14 minutes, while a [capacity-exhausted
run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/32939622815)
that ran
no training took about 16 minutes. A lower duration bound cannot
distinguish
these outcomes.

Set the minimum to zero and retain the 195-minute maximum. The
workflow's step
and loss checks still gate training quality.
[#8718](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8718) must land
first
because it makes capacity exhaustion fail explicitly.

Co-authored-by: yoblin <268258002+yoblin@users.noreply.github.com>
